subject: Climate & Environment
title: Your Home's Hidden Pollutants
description: A quick, practical guide to Your Home's Hidden Pollutants.

hook.text: Indoor air can be 2 to 5 times more polluted than outdoor air. And you spend 90% of time inside.

buildup.text: Cooking, cleaning products, candles, and furniture all release chemicals indoors.

discovery.text: Volatile organic compounds — VOCs — evaporate from paint, carpet, and glue for years.

twist.text: Modern homes are built airtight for energy efficiency, which traps pollutants inside.

climax.text: Opening windows for 10 minutes can cut indoor pollutant levels dramatically.

punchline.text: The most polluted room might be the one you're sitting in.

quiz.question: How does indoor air compare to outdoor air in pollution levels?
options: Indoor air can be 2-5 times more polluted

details.summary: Indoor air often contains higher pollutant concentrations than outdoor air due to building materials, furniture, cleaning products, and personal care items off-gassing volatile organic compounds, formaldehyde, and flame retardants in enclosed spaces.
details.whyItMatters: People spend roughly 90 percent of their time indoors, making indoor pollution a major but underappreciated health risk. Simple actions like ventilating and choosing low-VOC products help.
takeaways: Indoor air can be 2 to 5 times more polluted than outdoor air
New furniture and carpets off-gas formaldehyde and VOCs
Opening windows and using low-emission products reduce exposure

faq.question: What household products release the most VOCs?
faq.answer: Paints, varnishes, cleaning sprays, air fresheners, and new furniture are top VOC sources. Some release chemicals for months after purchase, a process called off-gassing, which increases concentrations in poorly ventilated rooms.

faq.question: How can you improve indoor air quality at home?
faq.answer: Open windows regularly, use exhaust fans in kitchens and bathrooms, choose low-VOC paints and products, avoid air fresheners, and maintain HVAC filters. These steps can reduce indoor pollutant levels significantly.
